question: Following the common agricultural policy (CAP) reform, each Member State designed a national CAP Strategic Plan for 2023-2027 and now, agriculture in the outermost regions as well as metropolitan France is subject to the obligations set out in this five-year programming document.

It has consequently become clear that the minimum surface area criteria set out in France’s CAP Strategic Plan for 2023-2027 are not particularly applicable to overseas territories, especially Mayotte. Before it was implemented, the national CAP Strategic Plan for 2023-2027 should have been adapted to include a specific plan for the archipelago of Mayotte, where the average size of a farm is 1.7 hectares (i.e.

130 square metres) In some cases, the Commission suggests surface area quotas that are incompatible with territories where the size of a farm is measured in hectares, not square metres. However, national Strategic Plans can be updated at any time. For example, France’s Strategic Plan has already been modified in recent months as a result of the effects of the Russia-Ukraine war.
Can the Commission and the French state work together to reform the national Strategic Plan’s calculation rule for Mayotte, where the size of agricultural holdings is much smaller?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.3.2024) Under shared management, Member States - the Managing Authority of each Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan - are responsible for setting minimum criteria to receive income support in their CAP Strategic Plan. The Commission assesses the adequacy of the strategy proposed by the Member State as well as the consistency with the legal framework1.

In the case of the French CAP Strategic Plan, the minimum criteria to receive income support is not area-based but financial (minimum EUR 200). Nonetheless, it is important to recall that CAP direct payments do not apply to the Outermost Regions (OR). They receive support from the POSEI2 instrument (together with certain market measures) which is not part of the French CAP Strategic Plan.

The basic aid allocated in the French POSEI programme to Mayotte takes specifically into account the small size of farms. Farms between 0.1 and 0.5 hectares receive EUR 450 a year with potential top-ups for newcomers, specific productions or for membership of a collective structure.

In addition, for rural development, various interventions (such as support for investments or conversion to organic farming) are specifically designed for ORs in the French CAP Strategic Plan with an increased support rate (up to 85%). Those interventions are designed by the Managing Authority in collaboration with the Regions.
1 Articles 118 and 119 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 establishing rules for the CAP Strategic Plans. 2 Programme of options specifically relating to remoteness and insularity.
